title: The Haagerup VOA at $c=8$
comment: Initial announcement. A full manuscript with complete details is forthcoming and will replace this announcement. The working manuscript and certificates are available at https://github.com/Doctorfm98/Haagerup_VOA . AI was used extensively in the discovery, and the author welcomes community feedback on the presentation and appropriate attribution
summary: We announce an explicit construction of a unitary, strongly rational vertex operator algebra $U$ of central charge $8$ inside $V_{E_6\oplus A_2}$, with a ribbon equivalence $\mathrm{Rep}(U)\simeq Z(\mathcal H_3)$ realizing the Haagerup double. The vertex algebra is generated by six affine currents and three specified weight-two fields; its weight-one Lie algebra is $\mathfrak{sl}_2\oplus\mathfrak{sl}_2$, at levels $1$ and $39$. We outline the argument, which combines exact lattice calculations, an all-weight strong-generation induction and $C_2$-cofiniteness, semisimple descent for a full corner of Zhu's algebra, modular Galois symmetry, and holomorphic $E_8$ extensions.

title: Dynamical Lie Algebras for Fixed-Gate Quantum Ansätze
comment: 21 pages, accepted as a poster at the QTML Conference
summary: Parameterized Quantum Circuits have emerged as a central framework for variational quantum algorithms in the NISQ regime, with major applications in quantum simulation, combinatorial optimization, and, more recently, quantum machine learning (QML). By developing a new approach for computing dynamical Lie algebras associated with quantum circuits combining parametrized gates and non-parametrized entangling gates, we aim to extend the applicability of recent algebraic results to architectures that are actually used in quantum machine learning.

title: Haar measure for totally positive split real semisimple quantum groups of classical type
summary: Let $\hbar$ be a non-zero real number and put $q= e^{-πi \hbar}$. Let $G$ be a semisimple split real Lie group of classical type, with Lie algebra $\mathfrak{g}$ and associated Borel subalgebra $\mathfrak{b} \subseteq \mathfrak{g}$. We show that there exists a locally compact quantum group $(L_{\hbar}(B),Δ)$ which integrates the Borel part $U_q(\mathfrak{b})$ of the Drinfeld--Jimbo quantized enveloping algebra $U_q(\mathfrak{g})$, viewed as a Hopf $*$-algebra. We further compute the associated Haar weights and modular data for $(L_{\hbar}(B),Δ)$. Up to an excess Cartan part, the Drinfeld double of $(L_{\hbar}(B),Δ)$ can be seen as an analytic quantization of the function algebra of the totally positive semigroup $G^+\subseteq G$.

title: Symmetries of colored Khovanov-Rozansky homology
summary: We construct an action of the positive half of the Witt algebra on colored $\mathfrak{gl}_N$-Khovanov-Rozansky homology and prove that this action is compatible with the functoriality of colored link homology. To establish this result, we use Bar-Natan's framework of canopolies to formulate and prove the relevant statements at the level of tangles.

title: Lusztig Parameters and Factorizations of Determinantial Modules
summary: We give an explicit formula for the Lusztig parameters of determinantial modules over symmetric quiver Hecke algebras. The formula applies to every Bruhat pair and every fixed reduced expression of the upper Weyl group element. In finite types $A$, $D$, and $E$, we identify the parameters of the modules in Ménard's seed using Demazure weaves. We then factor prefix determinantial modules into these seed modules, with multiplicities given by Lusztig cycles. We also give a criterion for recognizing monomials in this fixed seed and an explicit formula recovering their multiplicities from Lusztig parameters.

title: Right representations of Novikov algebras
summary:
We study the theory of right representations of Novikov algebras. We introduce the notion of a modular right ideal of a Novikov algebra and prove that every irreducible right representation of a Novikov algebra is isomorphic to the quotient by a maximal modular right ideal.
  We prove that the class of Novikov algebras with no irreducible representations forms a hereditary radical. We introduce the notion of a primitive Novikov algebra and show that a Novikov algebra is primitive if and only if it admits an almost faithful irreducible representation. We also introduce the notion of the quasi-kernel of a representation, defined as the largest ideal contained in its kernel. Finally, we prove that the constructed radical coincides with the intersection of the quasi-kernels of all its irreducible representations.

title: Galois actions on surfaces and a higher genus Grothendieck-Teichmüller group
comment: 81 pages; revisions, with the most substantial in Section 6
summary: We construct a modular operad $\mathbf{S}$ of mapping class groupoids modelling the higher-genus Teichmüller tower, with compositions and contractions encoding surface gluing. We prove a presentation theorem for maps out of $\mathbf{S}$ using genus-zero and genus-one generators and relations. Applying the work of Nakamura--Schneps, we obtain a faithful action of their subgroup $\widehatΓ\subseteq \widehat{\mathsf{GT}}$ on $\widehat{\mathbf{S}}$, and hence a faithful Galois action. The genus-zero truncation identifies with the cyclic operad of parenthesized ribbon braids, whose object-fixing profinite automorphism group is $\widehat{\mathsf{GT}}$. The completed classifying spaces form a modular $\infty$-operad whose corolla values are geometric étale homotopy types of moduli stacks of curves with nonzero tangent vectors at their marked points. The $\widehatΓ$-action induces a faithful action by homotopy automorphisms on the associated tower of profinite homotopy $1$-types, which agrees with the étale model in genus zero and one.
